meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did my son's essay get a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with him first, so did you?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. You still haven't said whether you spoke to him before the zero. Whatever happens next, nothing goes on his record, and it stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Kids misremember quotes all the time. That's a mark off for a bad quotation, not a zero.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine, it isn't in the play. That still doesn't tell me who spoke to Owen before the zero went in. What are you proposing now?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. To put this behind him, Owen will do the rewrite. I want it in writing tonight, nothing on his file, and the rest of my questions will be in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. Put the room and the time in tonight's email, and I'll confirm from my end.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Owen will do a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school under 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. I still want a straight answer on who decided the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it was entered. I expect that written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight plus an answer on who decided and whether Owen was spoken to first; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: Showing her the quoted line and telling her to search the scene herself, because it was something she could check, and your answer to her misquote defence closed the gap.
What cost ground: You never answered her repeated question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, so it stayed open and kept her pushing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits late on the night before the essay was due, came very close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was spoken to, answer it in one plain sentence before showing the version history, so she has nothing left to press on.
